messages.subject_clean: Error in if (num_cores_to_use > num_cores_computer_has) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am attempting to run a time-stratified analysis with different DEC models for each time period. I have been able to create the BioGeoBEARS_run_object and see that it has all of my parameters:

BioGeoBEARS_run_object <- define_BioGeoBEARS_run()
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$trfn <- treefile
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$timesfn <- "timeperiods.txt"
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$geogfn <- geogfn
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$max_range_size <- max_range_size
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$min_branchlength <- 0.000001
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$include_null_range <- TRUE
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$areas_allowed_fn <- "geography.txt"

But when I go to do the runslow loop, I get the following error.

Your computer has 16 cores
Error in if (num_cores_to_use > num_cores_computer_has) { :
    missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

I have not been able to find anywhere in the run_object where I could place a TRUE/FALSE statement in running my analysis.

Any and all help with this would be greatly appreciated!

Best,

Brenen

...if one of these is not a number, you would get that error message. It says you have 16 cores so probably it's num_cores_to_use.

Cheers,
Nick

messages.subject: Error in running attemping to run a for loop
messages.subject_clean: Error in running attemping to run a for loop
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have a very nuanced, but annoying issue. I am attempting to write a for loop, where I write the timeperiods.txt file in R, such that I can pull one of the numbers from a uniform distribution. I am effectively trying to estimate where likelihood is maximized given a random start date, as a hypothesis testing framework given the tree. I have had success in this front and can run the code in its entirety, but when I place it into a for loop and specifically when I run the following code:

BioGeoBEARS_run_object <- section_the_tree(inputs=BioGeoBEARS_run_object, plot_pieces=FALSE, cut_fossils=FALSE)

I get this fatal error:

Error in section_the_tree(inputs = BioGeoBEARS_run_object, plot_pieces = FALSE,  :
  STOP ERROR in section_the_tree(): the timeperiods file *HAS* to have an oldest time that is older than the bottom node in your tree.  Use the function prt() to get a table of node ages for your tree. The oldest node age in your tree is: 159.103925948033. The times in your timeperiods file are: .' (note that the oldest age is 165.0)

If I run this:

BioGeoBEARS_run_object <- readfiles_BioGeoBEARS_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object)

and then immediately repeat the section_the_tree again, then it reads it in correctly. However, this above fatal stop error stops my for loop and doesnt allow my code to get to the next line that reads it in correctly. I have been trying to use the try() function, but that has not been working for this. Any and all help with this would be greatly appreciated.

Best,

Brenen

messages.subject: pdf plots on Jupyter notebook on a HPC
messages.subject_clean: pdf plots on Jupyter notebook on a HPC
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am running biogeobears on my university cluster and is running smoothly although kind of slow (177 tips and 9 ranges with max range size=5). It is running parallel with several cores and it takes about 20 hours for each model to run, any suggestion to improve this?

Additionally,  I am using jupyter notebook to run all and I haven't been able to export the pdf plots successfully. I am able to see them on the notebook but in a distorted and too compressed way.

I read a conversation related to a similar issue with the pdf plot here and tried to re-run the  pdf+plot scripts at once and nothing changed. I also tried to use graphics.off()
 instead of dev.off() .
I used the Psychotria script from the tutorial on the website but modified for my data.

Could someone help me please?

Thanks,

Serena A.

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] pdf plots on Jupyter notebook on a HPC
messages.subject_clean: [BioGeoBEARS] pdf plots on Jupyter notebook on a HPC
messages.body_plain:
Hi -- that seems pretty slow for just 9 ranges/5 max.  Maybe it is just something about running through a jupyter notebook?  You might actually do better at the command line on a desktop computer.

Re: pdfs -- the pdf() command opens a PDF, then all plots get written to it, then dev.off() closes the PDF writing, then you can open the PDF like any other PDF file.

All you need to do to get the pdf to look different is to change the height and width options in the pdf() command.

Cheers!
Nick

messages.body_plain:
​Hi everyone!

I am a beginner user on the Biogeobers package. For days, I have been trying to run a stratified analysis using my own data set on BiogeoBears and I have got stuck since while on this warning and Fatal error (below).

WARNING in chainsaw2: input tree had a 'root.edge', which crashes chainsaw2. Setting original_tree$root.edge=NULL.
FATAL ERROR in section_the_tree(): Your tree has 4 fossil tips older than 0.1 my!
But you have not turned on fossils by setting 'cut_fossils=FALSE' in section_the_tree().
Fossil tip names listed below:
[1] "Fossil_one"  "Fossil_two"
[3] "Fossil_three" "Fossil_four".
Error in section_the_tree(input = BioGeoBEARS_run_object, make_master_table = TRUE,  :
Further: Warning message: In section_the_tree(input = BioGeoBEARS_run_object, make_master_table = TRUE,  : WARNING in chainsaw2: input tree had a 'root.edge', which crashes chainsaw2. Setting original_tree$root.edge=NULL.

Please, could someone give me some advice on how to solve these problems?

Thanks in advance.​

--

messages.body_plain:
Hi -- the root thing is just a warning, you can ignore.

For the fatal error, like the error message message says:

Go to the line of the script with section_the_tree()

Add the option cut_fossils=FALSE to that command.  cut_fossils=FALSE means you won't cut out the fossils.

Re-run it.

Cheers!
Nick

PS (This option exists  because for various reasons, including minor computer number rounding issues, people can have tree tips that don't quite come up to 0.000 million years before present, but they don't intend these to be fossils.)
